title: BitTrade Scorer: scenario planner for INT8 / FP8 / 4-bit
body:
Overview:

This working doc introduces the 'BitTrade' scorer — a compact, spreadsheet-friendly scoring heuristic to compare quantization choices (INT8, FP8, 4-bit) across cost, latency, and quality for production inference workloads. The goal is to provide product and infra owners a small decision surface they can use to quickly choose quantization families and safe rollouts based on measured evals and latency traces.

Audience and scope:
- Primary: product-optimize, serving-runtime, infra, and solutions engineering teams doing model serving cost optimizations.
- Scope: model variants targeted for serving (7B, 13B, 70B), online LLM workloads with SLOs (p99 latency targets, token budget), and offline batch embed workloads.
- Not in scope: model architecture search, training-time quantization-aware training experiments.

Design principles:
1) Simplicity: 1 numeric score that combines cost, latency, and quality differences so non-ML teams can rank choices.
2) Transparency: each component of the score is interpretable (savings or loss).
3) Tunable: weights can be adjusted per product line (e.g., chat vs bulk embedding).

Scoring formula (BitTrade v0.9):
- Inputs for each (model, quant) variant:
  - baseline_cost_per_1k_tokens (USD) — float
  - quant_cost_per_1k_tokens (USD) — float
  - baseline_p99_latency_ms (ms)
  - quant_p99_latency_ms (ms)
  - baseline_quality_score (higher is better, e.g., normalized QA accuracy, or 1 - relative PPL)
  - quant_quality_score

- Derived metrics (spreadsheet formula style):
  - cost_savings_pct = (baseline_cost_per_1k_tokens - quant_cost_per_1k_tokens) / baseline_cost_per_1k_tokens
  - latency_savings_pct = (baseline_p99_latency_ms - quant_p99_latency_ms) / baseline_p99_latency_ms
  - quality_loss_pct = (baseline_quality_score - quant_quality_score) / baseline_quality_score

- Score (higher is better):
  - score = w_cost * cost_savings_pct + w_latency * latency_savings_pct - w_quality * quality_loss_pct
  - default weights for general-purpose workloads: w_cost=0.4, w_latency=0.3, w_quality=0.5 (note quality penalized more; can be tuned per product)
  - normalize score to range roughly [-1, 1] in the spreadsheet by dividing by (w_cost + w_latency + w_quality) if desired.

Interpreting scores:
- score > 0.25: strong candidate for production rollout (subject to A/B eval).
- 0 <= score <= 0.25: marginal candidate; consider canary with strict rollback and hard quality checks.
- score < 0: do not roll out (quality degradation outweighs savings).

Example scenario table (CSV-friendly rows you can paste into a sheet):

scenario_name,model_name,baseline_cost_per_1k_tokens,quant,cost_per_1k_tokens,baseline_p99_ms,quant_p99_ms,baseline_quality,quant_quality,cost_savings_pct,latency_savings_pct,quality_loss_pct,score
chat-s1,redwood-open-7b,0.018,INT8,0.011,120,95,0.87,0.865,0.3889,0.2083,0.0138,0.4*0.3889+0.3*0.2083-0.5*0.0138
chat-s1,redwood-open-7b,0.018,FP8,0.013,120,100,0.87,0.868,0.2778,0.1667,0.0230,0.4*0.2778+0.3*0.1667-0.5*0.0230
embed-bulk,redwood-open-13b,0.045,4bit,0.028,220,190,0.94,0.90,0.3778,0.1364,0.0426,0.4*0.3778+0.3*0.1364-0.5*0.0426
qa-small,gptx-70b,0.12,INT8,0.08,340,260,0.92,0.91,0.3333,0.2353,0.0109,0.4*0.3333+0.3*0.2353-0.5*0.0109

Note: the last column is a formula placeholder; in your sheet replace with explicit numeric evaluation.

Guidance for metric selection:
- Quality metric: pick a product-aligned metric (e.g., Exact Match / F1 for QA, embedding cosine drop on benchmark, human-rated helpfulness). Convert all quality metrics to a normalized [0,1] scale prior to the score.
- Latency: use p99 end-to-end token throughput or cold-start-sensitive percentile depending on SLOs. For chat, p99 response tail matters more; for embeddings, median may be sufficient.
- Cost: include all infra cost per token (GPU amort + memory footprints + infra overhead). If you have reserved capacity discounts, use effective marginal cost.

Safety margins and rollout rules (recommended):
1) Safety thresholds: require quality_loss_pct <= 1.5% absolute (or <= X relative depending on metric) for any canary.
2) Latency SLO: quant_p99_ms must be <= baseline_p99_ms * 1.15 for chat SLOs (configurable).
3) Progressive rollout: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with quality and infra checks at each step.
4) Auto-fallback: if quality regression alert triggers or p99 latency exceeds threshold, automatically route traffic back to baseline model.

Use cases and quick heuristics:
- Cost-first background batch (embeddings): prioritize 4-bit or aggressive INT8 if score positive; relax quality requirements (w_quality = 0.2).
- Latency-critical chat: bump w_latency to 0.4, w_quality to 0.6, and prefer FP8/INT8 combos that preserve quality.
- Mixed workloads on Dedicated pools: compute per-model score, then solve knapsack-style allocation for GPU slots (separate spreadsheet that uses score as utility).

How to integrate into existing Optimize tooling:
- Provide a CSV upload endpoint for eval results (model, quant, cost, p99, quality) that returns computed score and recommended action.
- Add a 'BitTrade' preset to Optimize UI with adjustable weights and safety thresholds.
- Hook scoring into rollout automation (console): recommended canary percent and automatic guardrails.

Open questions / assumptions:
- Does cost_per_1k_tokens account for accounting-level reserved capacity amortization? Need infra finance input.
- Which quality normalization should be canonical across products (we have different units for QA vs embedding similarity)? Propose building product-level converters maintained in Optimize.
- How to reflect user-perceived quality thresholds (human eval) into an automated score? Consider a penalty multiplier for any metric that shows non-linear human sensitivity.

Next steps / action items:
- (Owner: Maya) Create canonical CSV template and example sheet (due 2024-10-12).
- (Owner: Liam) Wire up cost-per-token calculator that pulls reserved vs on-demand accounting (due 2024-11-01).
- (Owner: Sofia) Add data ingest for p99 traces and normalize pipeline (due 2024-11-15).
- (Owner: Ravi) Prototype UI slider controls for weights and rollout safety in Optimize console (due 2024-12-01).

Appendix A: small worked example (numeric evaluation)
- Baseline: redwood-open-7b, cost 0.018 /1k, p99 120ms, quality 0.87
- INT8: cost 0.011 /1k, p99 95ms, quality 0.865
  - cost_savings = (0.018-0.011)/0.018 = 0.3889
  - latency_savings = (120-95)/120 = 0.2083
  - quality_loss = (0.87-0.865)/0.87 = 0.0057 (~0.57%)
  - score = 0.4*0.3889 + 0.3*0.2083 - 0.5*0.0057 = 0.1556 + 0.0625 - 0.0029 = 0.2152
  - Interpretation: marginally good – could proceed to a small canary with strong quality checks.

Appendix B: quick checklist for SRE before rollout
- Validate KV cache behavior with quantized kernels (cold vs warm cache token profiles).
- Spike test at target throughput; verify tail latency under realistic batch mixes.
- Check memory growth and OOM rate on quantized builds.

Document history and notes:
- v0.1 initial concept (2024-09-18)
- v0.5 added normalization and example table (2024-10-05)
- v0.9 tuned weights and added rollout guidance (2024-12-02)

Comments and feedback welcome in-thread or addable as inline notes in the sheet.
